column15: Independent bottler (Signatory Vintage Scotch Whisky Co., Pitlochry). Samples name Mortlach, Ardmore and Ledaig/Tobermory (distillery rows emitted below); "Signatory Unnamed Orkney" and "Signatory Unnamed Speyside" are undisclosed casks, left unresolved per brief rule 3.

Wikipedia confirms Diageo ownership and Speyside/Dufftown location. No Mortlach-specific peat statement found; peat=none inferred from Speyside's general unpeated house style (cited page states peat use is uncommon there), not from a Mortlach-specific source, so confidence kept low.

Official site confirms peating throughout the range: Legacy is lightly peated, Tradition/Triple Wood carry fuller peat smoke. Recorded as medium as the overall house style spans light-to-rich rather than one fixed level.

THE flagship worked example from the brief: Ledaig is the heavily-peated sibling brand of Tobermory distillery, produced in small quantities. Not the same as unpeated Tobermory - keep these two rows separate.
Core Tobermory is made from unpeated malted barley (Wikipedia). Its peated sibling is the separate "ledaig" brand row, same distillery.

Standard/core Arran releases are unpeated (Wikipedia). Peated "Machrie Moor" range handled via rule below - all 6 samples for this brand are just generic "Arran", so the core unpeated profile is what should apply absent a Machrie Moor mention.

Umbrella brand covering Nikka's blends (Days, Super) and single malts (incl. Yoichi) in this catalogue. defaultType left empty since the range spans blend and single malt. COULD NOT CONFIRM PEAT CHARACTER this session: Wikipedia's Nikka/Yoichi/Japanese-whisky articles are silent on it and nikka.com returned 403/no content. Left unknown rather than rely on memory. REVIEWER FLAG: Yoichi distillery is widely described in whisky literature as using peated malt (medium-ish smoky/robust house style) contrasted with the unpeated, fruitier Miyagikyo - if independently confirmed, add a rule `nikka / Yoichi / word / / <level> / 60`. Left unwritten here rather than invent a citation.
Core range is sherry-cask matured (oloroso/PX) and unpeated per Wikipedia. Explicit NAS "Peated" expression handled via rule below.

Mainstream blended Scotch (Distell/Burn Stewart per general knowledge, not independently verified this session - no working source found). No distillery-specific peat statement found; defaulted to unpeated per the cited page's general point that peat is an optional, non-universal choice in Scotch production.
Wikipedia confirms Bacardi/Dewar's ownership; no peat statement there, defaulted to unpeated per ordinary-blend category norm.

Real Swedish distillery in Arboga (agitatordistillery.com, "Agitator ar ett svenskt destilleri i Arboga"). Could not confirm peat level of any expression, so left unknown (no citation opened to support none/light/medium/heavy - sourceUrls therefore left empty per the peatProfile=unknown rule). REVIEWER FLAG: "Agitator Rok" - "rok"/"rok" resembles Swedish "rok" (smoke); this sample may be a smoky/peated expression but I could not verify it, so no rule was written - worth a manual check.

Working distillery in the Wicklow Mountains, Ireland. Official site confirms an unpeated core range (pot still, single grain, single malt, various cask finishes). Explicit "Pot Still Peated" expression handled via rule below.

Mainstream Diageo blend (Arthur Bell & Sons, per general knowledge - dedicated Wikipedia page returned 404 this session). No distillery-specific peat statement found; defaulted to unpeated per ordinary-blend category norm. "Bell's Spiced" is a spiced/flavoured variant, not a peat indicator - no rule needed.

Brooklyn, NY brand; official site describes proofing/finishing sourced whiskey with Rosendale-mine limestone water rather than a full grain-to-bottle claim, so kept as kind=blend rather than distillery. Range spans bourbon and rye (defaultTypeName left empty). No peat mentioned; peat=none per general American-whiskey category norm (peat is rarely used outside Scotland, per the cited page).

Budget blended Scotch. One sample is literally "Highland Mist Loch Lomond", suggesting a Loch Lomond Group connection, but Loch Lomond distillery's own Wikipedia product list does not mention this brand, so owner is left empty rather than guessed. Peat=none per ordinary-blend category norm.
Wikipedia confirms Pernod Ricard/Chivas Brothers ownership and Speyside location. No distillery-specific peat statement; defaulted to unpeated per Speyside's general house style.
Core blend is unpeated per Wikipedia (William Grant & Sons ownership since March 2025). Peated "Smoky Black" (formerly Black Grouse) variant handled via rule below.
Own-label budget blend, no web presence found. Peat=none per ordinary-blend category norm. Samples include a "Skottish Collie" misspelling, added as a bonus alias.

Diageo's own single-malt showcase series for small/blending-malt distilleries it owns (not a third-party independent bottler in the strict sense, but modelled the same way since it spans several distilleries with no single peat profile). Distillery rows emitted below for all 4 samples: Auchroisk, Glen Spey, Inchgower, Mannochmore.
Wikipedia confirms Speyside/Diageo. No distillery-specific peat statement; defaulted per Speyside general house style.
Wikipedia confirms Speyside/Diageo; uses purifiers for a lighter spirit. No distillery-specific peat statement; defaulted per Speyside general house style.
Wikipedia confirms Speyside (Buckie)/Diageo. No distillery-specific peat statement; defaulted per Speyside general house style.
Wikipedia confirms Speyside/Diageo. No distillery-specific peat statement; defaulted per Speyside general house style.

Official site: "a blend of select malt and grain whiskies, matured in ex-bourbon oak barrels" (Belfast brand, revived by Belfast Distillery Company). No peat mentioned; peat=none per Irish-whiskey category norm.

Independent bottler (Speciality Drinks Ltd / Elixir Distillers / The Whisky Exchange group); England-based per general knowledge, not independently re-verified this session (low confidence on countryCode specifically). Samples name Port Askaig (own row below), Macduff and Teaninich (distillery rows below); "Speciality Drinks Speyside Marriage of cask" names no specific distillery and is left unresolved.

Wikipedia confirms this is an Islay single malt range bottled by Elixir Distillers from an officially undisclosed source distillery. Did not find a citation for Port Askaig's own peat level (only that it is marketed as Islay malt, and not every Islay distillery is peated), so left peatProfile=unknown per brief rule 3 rather than assume heavy. kind=blend since parentSlug cannot be set (source undisclosed).

Wikipedia confirms Highland region and Bacardi/Dewar's ownership, but has no peat statement. Unlike Speyside, the Highland peat citation I found does not support a blanket "unpeated" default (it describes normal Highland whisky as having peat up to 30ppm), so left unknown rather than guess.

Wikipedia confirms Highland/Diageo; mainly produces blending malt for Johnnie Walker Red Label. No peat statement found; left unknown for the same reason as Macduff (Highland peat is not a safe blanket default).

Iowa craft distillery; range spans bourbon and wheat whiskey per samples (defaultTypeName left empty). Could not load their own site this session (DNS/403 errors on several domain guesses). Peat=none per general American-whiskey category norm (cited page: peat rarely used outside Scotland), confidence kept low since not distillery-specific.

Wikipedia confirms South Ayrshire (Lowland)/William Grant & Sons and that it is a grain-whisky distillery. Grain whisky is conventionally unpeated, but the grain-whisky Wikipedia page I opened explicitly does not state this, so left peatProfile unknown rather than assert none without a supporting citation.

King Robert II budget blended Scotch. Checked Inver House Distillers' Wikipedia page on the assumption they own it; King Robert II is NOT listed among their brands there, so owner is left empty rather than asserted. Peat=none per ordinary-blend category norm.

Heaven Hill Quality House Old Style White appears to be a bottling/export label of Heaven Hill's Old Style White product. defaultTypeName left empty (mashbill/style of "Old Style White" unclear from samples). Peat=none per general American-whiskey category norm.

Family-owned Kentucky distillery, HQ Bardstown, current production at the Heaven Hill Bernheim distillery, Louisville (bought from Diageo in 1999 after the 1996 fire). defaultTypeName left empty (range spans bourbon/rye/wheat whiskey). Peat=none per general American-whiskey category norm; no peat mentioned on the Wikipedia page.
Wikipedia confirms Diageo ownership and "a blend of about 40 malt and grain whiskies"; no peat statement, defaulted to unpeated per ordinary-blend category norm.

Could not identify what this producer actually is. Samples ("Whiskey and Apple Juice", "Penicillin (Пеніцилін) 11 порцій") read as a flavoured/cocktail-kit product line (Penicillin is a well-known Scotch cocktail) rather than a conventional whisky brand; no dedicated Wikipedia article found. REVIEWER FLAG: this is a different entity from the "bayadera" store already in this codebase (a Ukrainian retailer) - no technical collision since producers and stores are separate tables, but worth a human sanity check on whether these SKUs belong in the whisky KB at all.

John Crabbie & Co blended Scotch; commonly attributed to Halewood International but not verified this session (dedicated Wikipedia page 404'd), so owner left empty. "Crabbie and Cree" sample is unclear - possibly a set or a specific SKU name - not further resolved. Peat=none per ordinary-blend category norm.

Own-label, 2 products, no web presence found and no naming evidence (unlike e.g. "Scottish Collie"/"Highland Mist") pointing to a specific country of origin, so left unknown rather than assumed Scotch.

Canadian whisky brand. Owner commonly cited as Corby Spirit and Wine (Hiram Walker/Pernod Ricard) but not verified this session, so left empty. defaultTypeName set to "blend" as the closest closed-list fit for Canadian whisky (no dedicated category exists). Peat=none per general non-Scotch-whisky category norm.

Dublin wine & spirits merchant that owns the "Spot" whiskey range (Green Spot, Yellow Spot), distilled at Midleton. Modelled as a bottler since Mitchell & Son does not distill itself. Brand rows (green-spot, yellow-spot) and the underlying distillery row (midleton) emitted below.

Cork, Ireland. defaultTypeName left empty since Midleton's range spans pot still, grain and blended whiskey. Peat=none per general Irish-whiskey category norm (Irish Distillers does occasionally release peated experimental whiskey, but the core/Spot range is unpeated).
Wikipedia (disambiguation) confirms "an Irish pot still whiskey". Distilled at Midleton, owned/bottled by Mitchell & Son. Peat=none per Irish pot still/general category norm.

Sibling to Green Spot in Mitchell & Son's "Spot" range, also a Midleton single pot still whiskey. No page opened specific to Yellow Spot itself; inferred from Green Spot's confirmed pattern plus the general Irish-whiskey unpeated norm - confidence kept low.

Believed to be a Kentucky Straight Bourbon private label commonly sold in European discount retail (general market knowledge), but no dedicated source was found/opened this session, so defaultTypeName is left empty rather than asserted as bourbon. Peat=none per general American-whiskey category norm.

Blended Scotch from J&W Hardie, a historic Perth blending house (per sample "J&W Hardie Talisman"). NOT the same as Talisker distillery (Isle of Skye) - deliberately kept alias scope narrow to avoid any confusion. Owner not independently verified this session. Peat=none per ordinary-blend category norm.

Real working Welsh distillery in Abergwyngregyn, Gwynedd (began production 2017, first release 2021) per Wikipedia's "Welsh whisky" article. Could not confirm peat status via Wikipedia or their own site this session - left unknown rather than assumed unpeated, since the Welsh whisky industry is too new/undocumented here for a safe category default.

Bernheim Original, a straight wheat whiskey made by Heaven Hill at their (New) Bernheim distillery, Louisville. defaultTypeName left empty since "wheat whiskey" has no exact match in the closed type list. Peat=none per general American-whiskey category norm.
Wikipedia explicitly states Daftmill uses "un-peated malt". Farm distillery, Cupar, Fife (Lowland).
Could not identify this brand within the research budget (possibly an own-label or a transliteration artifact); left entirely unknown.

Sample "Hepp Tharcis Alsacien" suggests an Alsatian (France) distiller (Hepp is a known Alsace fruit-spirit/eau-de-vie house); could not confirm within budget whether they produce whisky specifically or its peat status - left unknown.

Single product "J.Riddle Peated" - could not identify a producer within budget. The product name itself asserts "Peated" but I found no independent source to cite, so left peatProfile=unknown rather than assert heavy/medium on the strength of the catalogue name alone (brief rule: never invent a citation). REVIEWER FLAG: name strongly implies a peated whisky - worth a manual peatProfile assignment once the producer is identified.
Could not identify this brand within budget; left entirely unknown.
Could not identify this brand within budget (possibly a small/regional producer); left entirely unknown.
Presumed Irish whiskey brand by name; could not find a dedicated source this session. Peat=none per general Irish-whiskey category norm, confidence low.

Richmond, Virginia craft distillery; official site lists bourbon, rye and corn whiskey with no peat mention. defaultTypeName left empty since range spans multiple types. Peat=none per general American-whiskey category norm.

Peanut-butter-flavoured American whiskey (California); an infused/flavoured product rather than a traditional distillery. Peat=none per general American-whiskey category norm; nothing suggests a peated base.
Could not identify this brand within budget; left entirely unknown.

Valdespino is a historic Jerez sherry bodega, not normally a whisky producer. The single sample "Malt" is likely a mislabelled/miscategorised catalogue entry (perhaps a sherry, or a whisky finished in a Valdespino cask attributed to the cask supplier). REVIEWER FLAG: this row may not be a whisky at all - recommend manual inspection of the underlying product rather than trusting this KB row.
